knowledge:
- key_parameters: Alist=First list of genomic region sets (GRanges objects) to test ;; Blist=Second list of genomic region sets (GRanges objects) to test against Alist ;; sampling=Logical value indicating whether to sample a fraction of the dataset to speed up calculations ;; fraction=The fraction of regions to keep when sampling is enabled (default 0.15) ;; ranFUN=The randomization function to use, such as "resampleGenome", "randomizeRegions", or "resampleRegions" ;; evFUN=The evaluation function to use, such as "numOverlaps" ;; ntimes=Number of permutations to perform (minimum 5000 recommended for reproducible results) ;; mc.cores=Number of cores to use for parallel processing ;; pvcut=P-value cutoff used when creating the association matrix ;; matrix_type=Type of matrix to plot, either "association" or "correlation" ;; window=The genomic window size around regions for local z-score calculation ;; step=The step size for local z-score calculation
- alternatives: regioneR=Use regioneR when performing simple pairwise association analyses between only two region sets. Prefer regioneReloaded when analyzing multiple region sets simultaneously, comparing z-scores across different tests, clustering association profiles, or performing dimensionality reduction.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have multiple genomic region sets (e.g., ChIP-seq peaks, CUT&RUN peaks, DNA-methylation profiles, or genomic mutations) and want to identify clusters of co-localization, evaluate positional dependencies, or visualize complex association patterns in a low-dimensional space.
- pitfalls: Raw z-scores from different pairwise tests cannot be directly compared because they scale with the square root of the number of regions in the query set; always use the normalized z-score (norm_zscore) for comparisons. Performing permutation tests on large eukaryotic genomes is computationally expensive; use sampling or parallelization (mc.cores) to manage runtime. Running resampleRegions without specifying a universe will automatically generate a universe from Alist, which may not accurately represent the genomic background.

workflows.name: crosswise_association_clustering
workflows.intent: Perform crosswise permutation tests between multiple genomic region sets, construct and cluster an association or correlation matrix, and visualize the results using heatmaps and dimensionality reduction.
input: Alist (list of genomic region sets as GRanges objects)
Blist (optional second list of genomic region sets as GRanges objects)
genome (GRanges or Seqinfo object representing the reference genome)
workflows.stages:
1. Run crosswise permutation tests using crosswisePermTest() to calculate associations.
2. Build the association matrix and perform hierarchical clustering using makeCrosswiseMatrix().
3. Extract hierarchical clustering objects using getHClust().
4. Plot the clustered association or correlation matrix using plotCrosswiseMatrix().
5. Visualize a single pairwise permutation test result using plotSinglePT().
6. Perform and plot dimensionality reduction (PCA, t-SNE, or UMAP) using plotCrosswiseDimRed().
workflows.code:
cw_Alien_ReG<-crosswisePermTest(Alist = AlienRSList_narrow, sampling = FALSE, mc.cores= 25, ranFUN = "resampleGenome", evFUN = "numOverlaps", genome = AlienGenome, ntimes= 1000 )
cw_Alien_ReG<-makeCrosswiseMatrix(cw_Alien_ReG, pvcut = 1)
plotCrosswiseMatrix(cw_Alien_ReG)
modX <- getHClust(cw_Alien_ReG,hctype = "rows")
modY <- getHClust(cw_Alien_ReG,hctype = "cols")
X<-modX$labels[modX$order]
Y<-modY$labels[modX$order]
ord<-list(X=X,Y=Y)
p_ReG <- plotCrosswiseMatrix(cw_Alien_ReG, matrix_type = "association", ord_mat = ord)
p_ReR <- plotCrosswiseMatrix(cw_Alien_ReR, matrix_type = "association", ord_mat = ord)
plot(p_ReG)
plot(p_ReR)
plot(modX,cex = 0.8)
p_ReG_cor <- plotCrosswiseMatrix(cw_Alien_ReG, matrix_type = "correlation", ord_mat = ord)
plot(p_ReG_cor)
plotSinglePT(cw_Alien_ReG, RS1 = "regA", RS2 = "regA_05")
p_sPT1 <- plotSinglePT(cw_Alien_ReG, RS1 = "regA", RS2 = "regC")
plot(p_sPT1)
plotCrosswiseDimRed(cw_Alien_ReG, nc = 6, type="PCA")
p_cdr_hc <- plotCrosswiseDimRed(cw_Alien_ReG, nc = 6, type="PCA", clust_met = "hclust")
plot(p_cdr_hc)
lsRegSet<-list(regA="regA",regB="regB",regC="regC")
plotCrosswiseDimRed(cw_Alien_ReG, nc = 6, type="PCA",listRS = lsRegSet)
plotCrosswiseDimRed(cw_Alien_ReG, nc = 6, type="PCA",listRS = lsRegSet,ellipse = TRUE, emphasize =TRUE)
plotCrosswiseDimRed(cw_Alien_ReG, nc = 6, type="tSNE",listRS = lsRegSet,ellipse = TRUE, emphasize =TRUE)
plotCrosswiseDimRed(cw_Alien_ReG, nc = 6, type="UMAP",listRS = lsRegSet,ellipse = TRUE, emphasize =TRUE)
silTable <- plotCrosswiseDimRed(cw_Alien_ReG, nc = 6, type="UMAP",listRS = lsRegSet,return_table = TRUE)

workflows.name: multi_local_zscore
workflows.intent: Evaluate the positional dependency of a single genomic region set against a list of other region sets within a local genomic neighborhood.
input: A (a single genomic region set as a GRanges object)
Blist (a list of genomic region sets as GRanges objects)
genome (GRanges or Seqinfo object representing the reference genome)
workflows.stages:
1. Calculate local z-scores across a defined window and step size using multiLocalZscore().
2. Extract evaluation metrics and summary tables using getMultiEvaluation().
3. Generate a local z-score matrix and cluster the profiles using makeLZMatrix().
4. Plot the clustered local z-score matrix using plotLocalZScoreMatrix().
5. Plot individual or multiple local z-score profiles using plotSingleLZ().
workflows.code:
mlz_Alien_ReG<-multiLocalZscore(A = AlienRSList_narrow$regA, Blist = AlienRSList_narrow, ranFUN = "resampleGenome", evFUN = "numOverlaps", window = 100, step = 1, max_pv = 1, genome = AlienGenome)
getParameters(mLZ_regA_ReG)
mlz_Me <- getMultiEvaluation(rR = mLZ_regA_ReG )
head(mlz_Me$resumeTable)
mLZ_regA_ReG <- makeLZMatrix(mLZ_regA_ReG)
plot(getHClust(mLZ_regA_ReG),cex = 0.8)
plotLocalZScoreMatrix(mLZ_regA_ReG, maxVal = "max")
plotSingleLZ(mLZ = mLZ_regA_ReG, RS =c("regA"), smoothing = TRUE)
plotSingleLZ(mLZ = mLZ_regA_ReG,RS =c("regA","regA_02","regA_06","regA_08","regD"),smoothing = TRUE)
